description: Causal/predictive queries where context lacks causal evidence - system should mark as QUALIFIED

cases.query: Why do users prefer dark mode?
contexts: Survey data shows 82% of users have dark mode enabled on their devices.
Dark mode adoption has increased 340% since 2019 across all major platforms.
cases.description: Causal 'why' question with only correlational data
cases.rationale: Causal 'why' question but context only shows correlation/stats, no explanation of WHY

cases.query: Why did the stock price drop yesterday?
contexts: The stock closed at $142.50, down 8.3% from the previous day's close of $155.40.
Trading volume was 3x the 30-day average, with 45 million shares exchanged.
cases.description: Asks for cause but context only provides price data
cases.rationale: Asks for cause but context only provides price data, no explanation

cases.query: What will the weather be like next week?
contexts: Last week saw temperatures ranging from 65-78°F with partly cloudy skies.
Historical data shows October averages 68°F with 3.2 inches of rainfall in this region.
cases.description: Prediction question with only historical data
cases.rationale: Prediction question but context only has historical data, no forecast

cases.query: Why is Python popular for data science?
contexts: Python is used by 68% of data scientists according to the 2024 Stack Overflow survey.
Major companies using Python for data science include Google, Netflix, and Spotify.
cases.description: Asks WHY popular but context only shows THAT it's popular
cases.rationale: Asks WHY popular but context only shows THAT it's popular

contexts: Employee satisfaction scores dropped from 4.2 to 3.1 on a 5-point scale over the past year.
During this period, the company implemented a return-to-office policy and restructured several departments.
Exit interviews mentioned concerns about work-life balance and career growth opportunities.
cases.description: Correlating events and symptoms but no confirmed causal link
cases.rationale: Context provides correlating events and symptoms but no confirmed causal link

cases.query: What impact will AI have on employment?
contexts: McKinsey estimates 30% of work activities could be automated by 2030.
Historical automation has created more jobs than it eliminated, though in different sectors.
Current AI adoption is highest in finance, healthcare, and manufacturing.
cases.description: Prediction question with estimates and history only
cases.rationale: Prediction question - context has estimates and history but no definitive answer

cases.query: Why do some startups fail while others succeed?
contexts: 90% of startups fail within the first 5 years according to Bureau of Labor Statistics.
Successful startups like Airbnb and Uber pivoted multiple times before finding product-market fit.
Common characteristics of failed startups include running out of cash and lack of market need.
cases.description: Context lists correlations and patterns but no proven mechanism
cases.rationale: Context lists correlations and patterns but no proven causal mechanism

cases.query: What will Bitcoin's price be in 2025?
contexts: Bitcoin reached an all-time high of $73,000 in March 2024.
Analyst predictions range from $50,000 to $200,000 depending on regulatory developments.
The next Bitcoin halving is expected in April 2024, historically followed by price increases.
cases.description: Prediction question with opinions and patterns only
cases.rationale: Prediction question - context has opinions and historical patterns but no certain answer

cases.query: Why do cities with more ice cream sales have higher crime rates?
contexts: Data shows a strong positive correlation (r=0.85) between ice cream sales and crime rates across US cities.
Both ice cream sales and crime rates peak during summer months.
Cities with populations over 500,000 show the strongest correlation between these variables.
cases.rationale: Classic correlation vs causation trap - context shows correlation but the actual cause is a confounding variable (hot weather)

cases.query: Why do children who eat breakfast perform better in school?
contexts: Studies show students who eat breakfast score 17% higher on standardized tests.
Breakfast-eating students have 25% fewer absences and better classroom behavior.
Schools with free breakfast programs see improved academic outcomes across all subjects.
cases.description: Correlation shown but breakfast may be proxy for other factors
cases.rationale: Context shows correlation but breakfast may be proxy for other factors (stable home, parental involvement, SES)
